chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from several of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said:
I asked him about slaughtering (al-dhaka), so he said: One does not slaughter except with a sharp blade. The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) forbade that.
ai.seo_question: What is the required condition for valid animal slaughter in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Istibsar* establishes the fundamental juristic condition that valid slaughter (*dhaka*) requires a sharp blade (*hadidah*), explicitly linking this ruling to the authority of Imam Ali (AS). It serves as a primary textual basis in Shia fiqh for distinguishing permissible slaughter from that performed with teeth or nails, emphasizing the physical sharpness and sharpness of the instrument to ensure a swift, humane cut.
